newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: CRH says optimistic about growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: CRH says optimistic about growth in 1997.

text.p: CRH Plc said on Tuesday that it was optimistic about growth in 1997, although it did not expect the exceptional rate of growth it achieved in 1996.
"We do expect a continuing flow of interesting development opportunities in all our regions, but not at the exceptional rate of 1996," CRH chief executive Don Godson said in a results statement.
Godson said CRH's unique spread and balance should ensure another year of progress in 1997.
The group reported a rise of 20 percent in pre-tax profit to 193.43 million Irish pounds in 1996, up from 160.45 million in 1995.
CRH said Ireland should remain strong in 1997 with continuing growth, but probably at more modest rate in the second half.
It expected Britain, having failed to achieve its promised lift-off in 1996, to show some signs of a welcome return to growth.

The group said European economic and monetary union pressures will constrain growth in most European economies, "... but we have not had the prolonged freeze-up of 1996 and should see further advances," CRH said.
In the U.S. it expect markets to level off in 1997 but anticipated gains from 1996 acquisitions.
CRH said its strategy of regional development generated acquisitions, investments and capital expenditure totalling 531 million Irish pounds in 1996.
